record.title: Narelle makes landfall in three states
record.detail: BOM said Narelle hit Queensland as a category 4 (20 Mar), the NT as a category 3 (22 Mar) and WA's North West Cape as a severe category 4 (27 Mar), travelling about 6,500 km; only the second system on record to hit all three states as a severe cyclone.

record.attribution: Allegations by the AFP; charges not yet tested in court

record.attribution: Allegations by the AFP; charges not yet tested in court

record.attribution: Figures as reported by the National Anti-Scam Centre

The AFP said its Operation Firestorm has contributed to 560 arrests and disruption of 15 scam centres in the region.

record.title: Clandestine drug lab found, six charged over AUD 39m cocaine
record.detail: AFP and ABF executed warrants at Kingsdale near Goulburn and in Sydney after 120 kg of cocaine was found in vehicle transmissions shipped from California; 44 kg cocaine and 2 kg meth found at an alleged lab. Six NSW men charged.

record.title: Record 2.7-tonne cocaine seizure (Operation Minjiang)
record.detail: AFP said 2.7 t of cocaine landed near Midge Point, Qld, was seized at a Londonderry property in western Sydney, bringing the operation to more than 3 t (street value about AUD 816 million); eight people charged.
record.attribution: AFP media release (with QPS, ABF, ACIC, AUSTRAC)

record.title: ASIO 2026 threat assessment keeps level at PROBABLE
record.detail: ASIO Director-General Mike Burgess kept the terrorism threat level at PROBABLE, warning of self-radicalising youths with blended nationalist, racist and anti-authority ideologies and alleging IRGC-linked actors were behind antisemitic attacks in Australia.
record.attribution: ASIO Director-General via Australian Security Magazine

record.title: Tranche 2 AML/CTF obligations take effect for professions
record.detail: AML/CTF obligations began applying on 1 July 2026 to lawyers, accountants, conveyancers, real estate professionals and precious-metal dealers; AUSTRAC opened enrolment on 31 March with a 29 July deadline, and an estimated 80,000-90,000 new reporting entities are expected.
record.attribution: Compliance-industry summary of AUSTRAC dates; entity estimate as stated by Legl

record.title: Killara man charged with laundering AUD 2.4m through construction firm
record.detail: The AFP charged a 45-year-old man from Sydney's North Shore with dealing in proceeds of crime, alleging he laundered AUD 2.4 million in syndicate cash through a construction business using false invoices between June 2024 and November 2025.
record.attribution: Allegations by the AFP; charge not yet tested in court

record.title: Nationwide Telstra outage disrupts 000 calls, trains and payments
record.detail: A Telstra outage from about 04:30 to 16:00 hit mobile and internet services in all states, disrupting some calls to the 000 emergency line, V/Line and NSW regional trains, the ARTC network and EFTPOS; Telstra blamed a time-synchronisation software defect and the minister said ACMA would investigate.
record.attribution: SBS News; cause as stated by Telstra

record.title: Secondary Telstra fault hits 000 calling
record.detail: Following the 8 July outage, a secondary fault caused error messages on calls to the 000 emergency line; Telstra said it had cut occurrences by about 90% overnight, and the report said over 100,000 customers were potentially affected.

record.title: Seized Myanmar scam compound shows romance scams aimed at Australians
record.detail: ABC reported that the Shunda Park compound in Myanmar's Karen State, taken by the KNLA and holding about 3,000 workers, ran romance and investment scams; a freed worker said older Australian women were targeted. The UN estimates at least 120,000 people are trapped in Myanmar compounds.
record.attribution: ABC News report; figures attributed to the UN and researchers cited in the article

record.title: Man fined AUD 31,000 over botched reptile smuggling
record.detail: A NSW man was fined AUD 31,000 for exporting fauna without authority after 65 reptiles taken near Narembeen and Merredin were posted from WA; parcels were intercepted at Perth and 55 of the animals died or were euthanised.
record.agency: WA Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions

record.title: ACMA sues Optus in Federal Court over 2025 Triple Zero outage
record.detail: ACMA began Federal Court action alleging Optus Mobile breached emergency-call rules on 1,005 occasions during the 18 September 2025 outage; the maximum penalty is AUD 250,000 per contravention.
record.attribution: Allegations by ACMA; not yet determined by the court

record.title: H5N1 bird flu detected in tern at Portland, Victoria
record.detail: Agriculture Victoria said preliminary testing found high pathogenicity H5N1 avian influenza in a greater crested tern at Portland, following detections in seabirds in WA, SA, NSW and Queensland; the emergency animal disease response plan was activated and human risk was described as very low.
record.attribution: Claims by Agriculture Victoria (preliminary test result)

record.title: Five die in fiery head-on crash on Stuart Highway
record.detail: NT Police said a ute travelling at excessive speed crossed into the path of a van about 2km south of the Marrakai Road turn-off south-east of Darwin; both vehicles caught fire and all five occupants died.

record.title: AUSTRAC suspends Cryptolink, taking 96 crypto ATMs offline
record.detail: AUSTRAC suspended crypto ATM operator Cryptolink for three months, taking 96 machines offline, citing failures to lodge threshold transaction reports and weak ML/TF risk assessment; the firm had paid an AUD 56,340 infringement notice in 2025.
record.attribution: Crowdfund Insider report of AUSTRAC action; reasons as stated by AUSTRAC

record.title: Overhead wires fall on train, disrupting Sydney rail network
record.detail: Overhead wires came down on a South Coast Line train between Redfern and Erskineville around 16:30, isolating power on several tracks; hundreds of passengers were removed from three trains and services across Sydney were disrupted into the night.

record.title: 60 arrested in China-Australia tobacco smuggling takedown
record.detail: ABF and China Customs' Anti-Smuggling Bureau said Project Seahorse / Operation Trailblazer led to more than 60 arrests in China and seizure of over 60 million cigarettes in 91 containers bound for Sydney and other ports, with AUD 92 million in duty evaded.

record.title: Telcos issue new 000 calling advice after outages
record.detail: The Australian Telecommunications Alliance launched advice for calling the 000 emergency line during outages: hang up and redial if not connected within five seconds, then stay on the line up to a minute so the phone can find another network.
record.attribution: Advice issued by the Australian Telecommunications Alliance, as reported by EFTM

record.title: Bondi antisemitism royal commission ends hearings
record.detail: The Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion, set up after the 14 Dec 2025 Bondi Hanukkah attack that killed 15, closed hearings after 346 witnesses and over 20,000 submissions; final report due 18 Dec 2026.
record.agency: Royal Commission on Antisemitism and Social Cohesion

record.title: Two new Evolved Cape patrol boats commissioned in Cairns
record.detail: Navy commissioned HMAS Cape Spencer and HMAS Cape Hawke at HMAS Cairns for border protection and maritime constabulary work, with range over 4,000 nm.

record.title: Review finds Telstra failed to prioritise timing system behind July outage
record.detail: An independent review found the 8 July outage stemmed from a software update not applied to a GPS timing card; more than 600 calls to the 000 emergency line were unsuccessful. An ACMA investigation is ongoing, with fines of up to AUD 30 million possible.
record.attribution: SBS News; findings of the Telstra-commissioned independent review

record.title: Strike Force Myddleton: 33 charged over alleged AUD 600m loan fraud
record.detail: NSW Police allege a syndicate used false loan documents and inflated property deals to obtain up to AUD 600 million in loans, about AUD 500 million from the big four banks; 33 people have been charged and AUD 95 million in assets recovered, with the NSW Crime Commission, ATO and AUSTRAC involved.
record.attribution: Allegations by NSW Police as reported by ABC News

record.title: Optus outage blocks dozens of 000 calls in four jurisdictions
record.detail: An Optus network issue on a Friday caused intermittent call dropouts in Victoria, South Australia, Tasmania and the Northern Territory; about 39 calls to the 000 emergency line had connection difficulties, plus 3 in Tasmania.
record.place: Victoria, South Australia, Tasmania, Northern Territory

record.title: Late flu peaks recorded in several states
record.detail: ABC reported late-season influenza rises: Queensland recorded about 3,435 cases in one week and Victoria a 400% rise over seven weeks, though national notifications remain well below 2025, when over 1,700 influenza-related deaths were recorded.
record.attribution: ABC News citing the Australian CDC and state health departments

record.title: Mildura-area outage leaves 2,700 customers without power for days
record.detail: A ute hit a critical power pole at Birdwoodton, cutting power to more than 2,700 homes and businesses from about 06:30 on 21 September; Powercor pushed restoration back to Friday.

record.title: Security and ground-staff strikes hit Sydney and other airports
record.detail: About 400 Certis security staff at Sydney Airport held two-hour stoppages and TWU ground-service workers at Qantas subsidiaries began a 24-hour strike across Sydney, Adelaide, Brisbane and Perth; Qantas said it had contingency plans.
record.attribution: ABC News citing the TWU, Sydney Airport and Qantas

record.title: Bus with 18 aboard crashes on Melba Highway near Glenburn
record.detail: A public-transport bus carrying 17 passengers and a driver collided with two cars on the Melba Highway near Glenburn; a car driver died and six people were injured, two seriously.

record.title: Dhaka ranked world's most polluted major city, AQI above 250
record.detail: IQAir reported Dhaka's AQI above 250 (hazardous range) on 14 January, ranking it the most polluted major city, citing brick kilns, traffic and construction dust amid stagnant winter air.

record.title: HRSS: 10 killed, 2,503 hurt over election period; polling day largely peaceful
record.detail: Human Rights Support Society counted over 700 election-related violence incidents from October 2025 to 14 February 2026, with 10 dead and 2,503 injured; its observers logged 393 polling-day irregularities including 105 supporter clashes but no polling-day deaths.

record.title: HRSS: 10 killed, 1,933 hurt in election-month violence
record.detail: Human Rights Support Society recorded 346 political violence incidents in February 2026, the month of the 13th parliamentary election, leaving 10 dead and 1,933 injured; most involved BNP-Jamaat clashes and intra-BNP feuds.

record.title: Train hits bus at Cumilla level crossing, 12 dead
record.detail: A Dhaka-bound train struck a bus that had entered the tracks at the Padua Bazar level crossing on the Dhaka-Chattogram highway, killing 12; rail traffic was suspended for about three hours and two gatemen were suspended.
record.attribution: Police and fire service via AIR

record.title: 13 fishermen seized on Naf River, allegedly by Arakan Army
record.detail: Thirteen Bangladeshi fishermen from Shah Porir Dwip were seized on the Naf River by armed men on speedboats, allegedly Arakan Army, and taken into Myanmar; BGB data cited says at least 399 fishermen have been taken since Dec 2024.
record.attribution: Daily Star commentary citing BGB data via New Age

record.title: Gas lighter factory fire kills 5 in Keraniganj
record.detail: A fire at a gas lighter factory in the Kadamtali area of Keraniganj killed at least five people; seven fire service units took several hours to control it and the cause was under investigation.
record.attribution: Fire Service and Civil Defence via AP

record.title: ~250 missing after Teknaf trawler sinks in Andaman Sea
record.detail: UNHCR and IOM said about 250 Rohingya and Bangladeshis were missing after an overcrowded trawler that left Teknaf for Malaysia sank in rough seas; nine were rescued on 9 April, six of whom were detained as alleged traffickers.
record.attribution: UNHCR and IOM joint statement via Al Jazeera

record.title: Load-shedding exceeds 2,000 MW; 15+ plants offline
record.detail: Power Grid Bangladesh figures showed supply of 13,198 MW against 15,200 MW demand, with over 15 plants shut by fuel shortages linked to Middle East disruption of LNG imports and faults; rural areas faced 8-10 hour outages during the heatwave.
record.attribution: Power Grid Bangladesh data via TBS

record.title: WHO: measles in 58 of 64 districts, 166 deaths
record.detail: WHO reported 19,161 suspected and 2,897 confirmed measles cases with 166 deaths between 15 March and 14 April 2026, across all eight divisions (Dhaka 8,263 cases); a nationwide measles-rubella campaign for children 6-59 months began 20 April and WHO rated national risk high.
record.attribution: World Health Organization, citing national surveillance

record.title: Mild-to-moderate heatwave; Jashore peaks at 38°C
record.detail: BMD said a mild-to-moderate heatwave covered Khulna division, Dhaka, Rajshahi and other districts, with a high of 38°C in Jashore, and could begin to ease with rain; power supply ran about 200 MW short at peak.

record.title: Two Bangladeshis killed by BSF pellet fire, Kasba
record.detail: BGB said two Bangladeshi men, part of a group of about 15 alleged smugglers who crossed into India, died in an Indian hospital after a BSF member fired pellets during a scuffle near the Dhajanagar-Pathariyadwar border late on 8 May.
record.attribution: BGB account via The Daily Star

record.title: Measles deaths among children pass 500
record.detail: Al Jazeera reported the health department tally at 512 child deaths from measles since 15 March 2026, with Dhaka hospitals overwhelmed; the outbreak is described as the deadliest in decades.
record.attribution: Bangladesh health department tally via Al Jazeera

record.title: UNHCR: 152,029 new Rohingya arrivals since Dec 2024
record.detail: UNHCR said 152,029 newly arrived Rohingya were registered between December 2024 and 31 May 2026, including 2,260 in May 2026, fleeing violence in Rakhine State; about 1.2 million Rohingya are in the camps.

record.title: M4.5 quake near Silchar felt in Dhaka and Sylhet
record.detail: BMD said a magnitude 4.5 earthquake at 10 km depth near Silchar, Assam, about 92 km east of Sylhet, was felt in Dhaka and elsewhere at about 21:40; no damage was reported.
record.place: Near Silchar (Assam), ~92 km E of Sylhet

record.title: Bangladeshi killed in BSF firing, Kulaura border
record.detail: A Bangladeshi villager was killed in BSF firing near border pillars 1852-1853 (Nishchintapur/Dattagram area); BGB 46 Battalion said BSF took the body to an Indian hospital morgue and would hand it over after legal procedures.
record.attribution: BGB 46 Battalion, local police via TBS

record.title: BGB blocks BSF push-in of 20 people, Shibganj
record.detail: BGB's Mahananda 59 Battalion said Chouka border outpost members prevented BSF from pushing 20 people into Bangladesh; the group remained on the Indian side at the zero line.

record.title: Quake centred at Rupganj jolts Dhaka
record.detail: An earthquake centred at Rupganj, Narayanganj, about 16 km northeast of Dhaka at 16 km depth struck at about 21:28; USGS put it at M4.4 and BMD at 4.0, with no immediate reports of casualties.

record.title: BFIU froze ~55,000 MFS accounts over gambling and hundi
record.detail: Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury told parliament the BFIU had suspended about 55,000 mobile financial service accounts suspected of online gambling and digital hundi; Bangladesh Bank issued MFS monitoring directives on 28 May.

record.title: RSF: 438 killed in 472 road crashes in June
record.detail: Road Safety Foundation counted 472 road crashes in June 2026 killing 438 and injuring 561; motorcycles accounted for 134 deaths and pedestrians 91.

record.title: Rights group: 10 Bangladeshis killed by BSF in H1 2026
record.detail: Ain o Salish Kendra said, based on newspaper reports, that 10 Bangladeshis were killed in BSF border violence in January-June 2026 (7 shot, 3 after torture), with 10 injured and 1 abducted across 21 incidents.
record.attribution: Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK), compiled from media reports

record.title: Chattogram records 412 mm in 24 hours, highest in 43 years
record.detail: BMD recorded 412 mm of rain in Chattogram in the 24 hours to 15:00 Tuesday, the highest 24-hour total in 43 years, from a Bay of Bengal low-pressure system; a further 179.4 mm fell over the next 24 hours.

record.title: Landslides kill 22 in Chattogram region over three days
record.detail: Landslides and wall collapses after record rain killed 22 people over three days in Cox's Bazar, Chattogram and Rangamati, including five madrasa students in Ukhiya when a retaining wall collapsed.

record.title: Landslides kill at least 18 Rohingya, mostly children
record.detail: At least 18 Rohingya, mostly children, were killed in landslides and a wall collapse at a madrasa in the Ukhiya and Teknaf camps; officials said more than 200 landslides and flash floods had destroyed thousands of shelters.
record.attribution: Refugee Relief and Repatriation Commission (RRRC) official via Arab News

record.title: FFWC: 10 districts at flood risk; Sangu 190 cm over danger
record.detail: FFWC warned of flooding in 24-72 hours in Feni, Chattogram, Khagrachhari, Sylhet, Netrokona, Sherpur, Mymensingh, Lalmonirhat, Kurigram and Gaibandha; the Sangu at Bandarban was 190 cm above danger level and the Matamuhuri at Lama 18 cm above.

record.title: FFWC: Surma-Kushiyara rising, Sylhet floods may worsen
record.detail: FFWC said the Surma at Chhatak, Kushiyara at Markuli and Fenchuganj, and Someshwari at Kalmakanda were above danger level and the flood situation in Sylhet, Sunamganj, Netrokona, Sherpur and Mymensingh could deteriorate over two days.

record.title: 300+ Bangladeshis repatriated from SE Asia scam compounds
record.detail: The Expatriates' Welfare Ministry said more than 300 Bangladeshis rescued from cyber scam compounds in Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam and elsewhere have been repatriated; survivors reported paying recruiters up to about Tk 900,000.
record.attribution: Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment via Dhaka Tribune

record.title: BFIU to freeze 14,000 more gambling-linked MFS accounts
record.detail: A BFIU official said 10,000 MFS accounts were frozen the previous month and a further 14,000 would be frozen on an agency report; the Gambling Prevention Act 2026 took effect 1 July.

record.title: Load-shedding surges past 2,000 MW amid gas and coal shortfalls
record.detail: PGCB data showed the power shortage rising from 335 MW on 6 Aug to 2,167 MW on 8 Aug, driven by coal-handling problems and insufficient gas to power plants; Pabna reported 8-10 hour outages and Khulna 3-5 hours daily.
record.attribution: Power Grid Company of Bangladesh (PGCB) data via The Daily Star

record.title: Monsoon depression: ports keep signal No. 3
record.detail: The Met office told Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla and Payra ports to keep local cautionary signal No. 3 as a monsoon depression intensified over the southwest Bangladesh-West Bengal coast; fishing boats in the North Bay were told to stay near the coast.

record.title: Chinese/Taiwanese-run online fraud base found in Cox's Bazar resorts
record.detail: CID said a group of Chinese and Taiwanese nationals rented resorts and a residential building near Himchhari along Marine Drive and set up soundproofed rooms with thousands of iPhones and computers for international online fraud; six were remanded under the Cyber Security Act 2026 and four others are fugitives.

record.title: RSF: 481 killed in 513 road crashes in August
record.detail: Road Safety Foundation, compiling media reports, counted 513 road crashes in August 2026 killing 481 and injuring 664; motorcycles accounted for 176 deaths and pedestrians 102, with Bogura the deadliest district (37).

record.title: BGB seizes 1.4 million yaba tablets at Hnila
record.detail: BGB's 64 Battalion (Hnila border outpost) said a patrol acting on intelligence about smuggling from Myanmar arrested two suspects near the zero line with 1.4 million yaba tablets.

record.title: 63 foreigners held at scam hub in Chattogram building
record.detail: Police arrested 63 foreign nationals (Chinese, Pakistani, Laotian, Nepali, Vietnamese) running an online fraud operation from a seven-storey residential building in Chattogram, seizing 134 phones and 57 laptops.

record.title: Court freezes Tk 786 crore of Nagad-linked shares
record.detail: On an ACC petition, Dhaka Senior Special Judge Md Shahjahan Kabir froze Tk 786 crore in shares linked to former Nagad MD Tanvir Ahmed Mishuk and associates; ACC alleges about Tk 1,706 crore in government allowance funds was diverted and laundered abroad.

record.title: Dengue: 5 deaths, 1,484 admissions in 24 hours
record.detail: DGHS reported 5 dengue deaths (4 in Dhaka North City Corporation, 1 in Rangpur division) and 1,484 hospitalisations in the 24 hours to 08:00; year-to-date 58,400 cases and 176 deaths, with 4,132 patients in hospital.

record.title: 480,000 yaba seized in Teknaf and Himchhari

record.title: Dengue death toll for 2026 passes 200

record.title: Flash floods hit Brunei-Muara and Tutong villages
record.detail: Prolonged heavy rain on Jan 7-8 caused rapid flooding of roads and homes in several Brunei-Muara mukims (Gadong, Berakas, Kilanas, Kota Batu, Kianggeh, Pengkalan Batu) and Tutong villages incl. Birau, Kebia and Bekiau; a vehicle was submerged on Jalan Aman, Berakas B. BDMD said wet conditions would persist to Jan 12.
record.attribution: BDMD advisories via Borneo Bulletin/ANN (The Star)

record.title: Rain-triggered landslide at Tutong cemetery
record.detail: Persistent heavy rain caused a landslide at the Luagan Kelupang Muslim cemetery in Kampong Sinaut; FRD, NDMC, the district office and Public Works inspected and covered the slope with canvas. No casualties reported.
record.attribution: Ministry of Religious Affairs via Borneo Bulletin/ANN (The Star)

record.title: Flooding slows Muara-Tutong Highway traffic
record.detail: Floodwater on sections of the Muara-Tutong Highway near Kampong Keriam caused long queues between Tutong and Brunei-Muara; a red weather advisory had been issued the night before for Belait, Tutong and western Brunei-Muara.
record.attribution: Motorist accounts and weather advisory via Borneo Bulletin/ANN (The Star)

record.title: Landslide severs main pipeline; Brunei-Muara water cut
record.detail: Public Works Department said a landslide at Batang Mitus, Tutong, damaged 16 sections of a main water pipeline, disrupting supply to Berakas, Gadong, Kota Batu, Kilanas, Kianggeh and Pangkalan Batu; clinics limited to urgent cases, some private schools closed, and water tanks deployed. Full restoration expected around Feb 2.

record.title: Central bank warns against unlicensed financial providers
record.detail: BDCB warned the public to deal only with licensed institutions, saying unlicensed entities increasingly advertise deposit-taking, lending, investment and remittance services on Facebook, Instagram, Telegram and WhatsApp.

record.title: Cable theft blamed for power disruptions
record.detail: Department of Electrical Services said outages on Mar 17 and 19 affecting Kampong Kasat, Kampong Sungai Liang, Mukim Seria and Kampong Kiarong followed damage to underground cables and equipment in attempted thefts; it warned such tampering carries 3-10 years' jail and caning.
record.place: Kampong Kasat, Sungai Liang, Seria, Kiarong

record.title: Highway cycling ban planned after cyclist deaths
record.detail: After two cyclist deaths and one hospitalisation in separate crashes over the previous month, the development minister outlined plans to ban cycling on highways and roads above 65 km/h (nine named roads incl. Muara-Belait Highway) and designate district cycling routes.
record.attribution: Minister of Development via The Scoop

record.title: Royal Brunei Airlines extends Dubai suspension
record.detail: Royal Brunei Airlines extended its suspension of Bandar Seri Begawan-Dubai flights until Jul 2, citing regional conflict and Gulf airspace closures, while keeping three weekly direct London flights.
record.attribution: Royal Brunei Airlines notice via TTR Weekly

record.title: Impersonation-scam 'runner' arrested
record.detail: RBPF arrested a 23-year-old foreign national suspected of collecting cash from victims who were threatened by syndicate members posing as government officers by phone; phones, a tablet and a vehicle were seized.

record.title: Heat drives surge in forest and bush fires
record.detail: FRD recorded 125 forest and 81 bush fires (about 415.5 ha) from Jan 26 to Apr 26, 88 forest fires in April alone; blazes near Universiti Teknologi Brunei (~28 ha, Apr 25) and RPN Kampong Rimba (~20 ha, Apr 26) needed RBAF water-bombing via NDMC.

record.title: 7-hectare fire at Berakas Forest Reserve
record.detail: A fire spreading in patches over hilly terrain burned about 7 ha of government land at the Berakas Forest Reserve recreational park; FRD sent four engines and 32 personnel. No injuries.

record.title: MoH: no hantavirus cases, risk low
record.detail: The Ministry of Health said Brunei had no hantavirus cases and low risk amid the MV Hondius cruise-linked cluster, advising travellers from affected areas with fever or respiratory symptoms to seek care.

record.title: High Court forfeits drug-syndicate assets
record.detail: On an NCB application, the High Court forfeited BND143,274.40 in cash, gold jewellery and vehicles from a couple linked to a family-run methamphetamine trafficking ring ('Musang King') arrested in 2020.

record.title: MoH rates Bundibugyo Ebola risk low
record.detail: MoH said the risk of Bundibugyo virus disease (Ebola) reaching Brunei is low and advised against non-essential travel to affected areas of DR Congo and Uganda, following WHO's PHEIC declaration.

record.title: Southwest monsoon begins; drier months forecast
record.detail: BDMD said the southwest monsoon (May-Sep) would bring more stable, possibly drier-than-normal weather, with August forecast at 140 mm or less; it cited a 92% chance of El Nino conditions.

record.title: 'BTC 800 Lurotix' added to BDCB Alert List
record.detail: BDCB added 'BTC 800 Lurotix' to its Alert List of unlicensed entities over suspicious activities and warned of scammers misusing the central bank's name and logo.

record.title: Malaysian jailed over cross-border ATM fraud
record.detail: A Malaysian man was jailed 6 years 8 months under the Computer Misuse Act for collecting debit cards in Brunei for accomplices' unauthorised ATM withdrawals on instruction from a Malaysia-based handler; losses BND8,480.

record.title: House fire kills girl in Seria
record.detail: A night fire gutted a wooden house in Seria and spread to an adjacent structure; a 9-year-old girl died and a 72-year-old suffered burns. FRD controlled it within an hour; cause under investigation.

record.title: Multi-agency operation in Bandar Seri Begawan
record.detail: Over 200 officers from RBPF, immigration, NCB, customs, labour and others checked two sites; two foreigners were held under the Immigration Act and labour/electricity breaches recorded. A trafficking unit interviewed 19 people and found no trafficking offences.

record.title: Chinese navy ships make port call at Muara
record.detail: PLA Navy training ship Qi Jiguang and landing ship Kunlunshan made a five-day goodwill visit (Jul 24-28) to Muara port, with public tours offered.

record.title: Belait joint operation: two held for drugs
record.detail: A 59-strong RBPF-led operation with NCB, customs and immigration in Kuala Belait detained two men on suspected drug offences; customs recorded 14 offences involving 12 people and seized 73 cigarette packets and a vape.
record.place: Jalan Kuala Balai / Jalan Pandan 5, Kuala Belait

record.title: Six foreigners detained in Seria immigration check
record.detail: Immigration (INRD) Operasi Kakas 79/2026 inspected 16 foreign nationals in Seria and detained six: five for working for employers not on their permits and one for overstaying.

record.title: Police warn of fake 'investigation notice' scam
record.detail: RBPF warned that fraudsters are sending forged 'Notice of Involvement in Investigation' letters and fake warrant cards impersonating its Cyber Crime Investigation Division and Interpol to extract money or bank details.

record.title: 14 straight days of excessive heat; 38.2C at Labi
record.detail: BDMD said Aug 8-21 brought 14 consecutive days of excessive heat, peaking at 38.2C at Labi (Anggerek Desa 37.5C); August rain to date was about 51% below normal and maxima of 33-36C were expected to continue.

record.title: 15 foreigners held in Operasi Kakas checks
record.detail: INRD reported four operations in Mukim Sengkurong and Berakas A/B inspecting 28 foreign nationals and detaining 15 for working on visit passes, overstaying or not working for their original employer.

record.title: Haze arrives; MoH advises vulnerable groups
record.detail: MoH, with BDMD, advised vulnerable groups to limit outdoor activity as smoke from 1,180-1,734 daily Borneo hotspots drifted in; PSI on Aug 30 was moderate (Brunei-Muara 73, Tutong 70).

record.title: HFM-linked entity added to BDCB Alert List
record.detail: BDCB added 'Goldpecker Community/HF Markets/HFM' to its Alert List for investment-related activity without BDCB licence.

record.title: MoH issues haze health advisory
record.detail: Following a joint ministerial statement, MoH warned haze can worsen asthma and heart and lung disease, and advised limiting time outdoors, well-fitted masks and HEPA purifiers.

record.title: Haze: Brunei-Muara PSI 116
record.detail: JASTRe's 09:00 PSI was unhealthy in Brunei-Muara (116) and Belait (107); PM2.5 was added to the PSI from Sep 1.
record.agency: Department of Environment, Parks and Recreation (JASTRe)

record.title: Belait PSI climbs to 152

record.title: Customs seize 4.25 kg of drugs at border posts

record.title: Haze returns to unhealthy in two districts

record.title: Climate-resilient bridge completed in flood-hit Dechencholing
record.detail: BBS reported a Nu 25 million, flood-resilient bridge was completed in Dechencholing, Thimphu, replacing hume pipes that blocked and overflowed; the area was devastated by an August 2024 flash flood.

record.title: Global roadshow for USD 190M Gelephu–Tareythang road and bridges project
record.detail: Kuensel reported an international roadshow began to attract contractors for the USD 190 million Gelephu–Tareythang road and bridges project, part of Gelephu Mindfulness City, including a 1,005 m bridge with elephant crossings.

record.title: M5.5 earthquake near Punakha damages 404 households
record.detail: BBS, citing the Department of Local Governance and Disaster Management, reported a 23:36 quake centred in Punakha (~20 km deep) damaged 404 households mainly in Wangdue Phodrang, Punakha and Monggar, plus schools and monuments; one person injured in Lhuentse, no deaths.
record.attribution: Department of Local Governance and Disaster Management via BBS

record.title: Recurring landslide debris floods Phuentsholing–Samtse highway at Amochhu
record.detail: BBS reported an active upstream landslide has washed debris onto the highway near the fuel depot almost nightly since mid-May, blocking traffic for hours; Phuentsholing Thromde said the problem exceeds its capacity and halted night clearance for worker safety.

record.title: Amochhu flooding disrupts exports and labour-permit processing
record.detail: BBS reported recurring Amochhu floods and road blockages delayed boulder exports and foreign-worker permits (2–3 days); Thromde said it had spent over Nu 2 million on clearance by 8 June and floodwater had entered the NHDCL housing colony.
record.attribution: Phuentsholing Thromde and labour agents via BBS

record.title: NCHM warns of extremely heavy rain over southern Bhutan
record.detail: NCHM issued a warning of heavy to very heavy rainfall over southern and isolated central areas valid 28–29 June 2026, following a 19 June advisory on very heavy rain in the south.
record.attribution: National Center for Hydrology and Meteorology warning

record.title: Overnight flooding in Phuentsholing displaces over 70 families
record.detail: Heavy rain on the night of 28–29 June flooded Chamkuna/Amochhu areas; BBS said over 70 families were displaced, 30+ evacuated from the Amochhu temporary settlement, a canteen destroyed and about 70% of ~1,300 LPG cylinders at Pemaling swept away; no casualties.

record.title: Flash flood washes away Bailey bridge, cutting off 75 households in Tsamang
record.detail: Evening flash flood in Ganglapong (Monggar) destroyed the only road bridge linking Tsamang gewog villages to Autsho; NCHM attributed it to heavy rain that may have partially breached the 2003 Tsatichhu landslide dam. No casualties.

record.title: OAG: SP+ capsules dominate drug trafficking cases in FY2025-26
record.detail: The Office of the Attorney General's annual report, as reported by BBS, said it handled 279 narcotics/psychotropic cases, 220 of them involving Spasmo Proxyvon Plus capsules; 31 involved brown sugar/heroin and 28 N10 tablets.
record.attribution: Office of the Attorney General annual report via BBS

record.title: Heritage Changyul Galem House collapses in Punakha
record.detail: The government acknowledged a conservation-funding gap after the nationally significant Changyul Galem House partially collapsed on 9 August; emergency stabilisation began 11 August. No casualties reported.
record.agency: Department of Culture and Dzongkha Development

record.title: PM: GLOF monitoring ongoing; Thorthormi siphoning pilot launched in Lunana
record.detail: PM Tshering Tobgay said Thorthormi and Rapstreng lakes pose the greatest threat; The Bhutanese reported 77 communities (1,196 households, 11,921 people) at risk across Gasa, Punakha, Wangdue and Tsirang, a siphoning pilot launched 9 Sept in Lunana and USD 22 million GCF support approved.
record.attribution: Prime Minister and NCHM figures via The Bhutanese

record.title: NCHM: fluctuating September rain and temperature swings amid El Niño
record.detail: NCHM forecast above-normal rain in early and late September with a drier, hotter mid-month in the south, and said a strong El Niño may persist to February 2027, with possible impacts on agriculture and hydropower.

record.title: GLOF preparedness in Samdingkha, Punakha; residents remain anxious
record.detail: BBS reported ~75 residents in 40 houses/shops at Samdingkha lie in the Phochhu GLOF path; 17 siren stations and 7 automatic water-level stations are installed along the Phochhu.

record.title: Thimphu police log 37 OTP/online-banking scam cases in two weeks
record.detail: The Bhutanese reported scammers used fake bank Facebook pages and a counterfeit app to capture logins and OTPs; Thimphu police received 37 cases in two weeks and froze accounts in most cases; one victim lost Nu 424,000, later largely recovered.

record.title: Air-quality concerns over Norbugang industrial park emissions

record.title: Traders allege goods from low-tax Sarpang smuggled to other districts

record.title: MND calls Diaoyu patrols legitimate after record 356 days in 2025
record.detail: Defence ministry spokesperson Zhang Xiaogang called CCG patrols near Diaoyu Dao lawful and urged Japan to show restraint, after Japanese reports that Chinese ships were present on 356 days in 2025.

record.title: HK Customs steps up action on unlicensed money services on social media
record.detail: Customs said it detected 23 unlicensed money-service cases in 2025 (22 on social media), arresting 24, plus 4 account holders suspected of laundering; one holder was jailed 54 months.
record.agency: Hong Kong Customs and Excise Department

record.title: PLA monitors first US Taiwan Strait transit of 2026
record.detail: Eastern Theater Command spokesperson Senior Col Xu Chenghua said naval and air forces tracked USS John Finn and USNS Mary Sears through the strait and that the command remained on high alert.
record.attribution: PLA Eastern Theater Command via Global Times (state media)

record.title: China executes 11 Ming family crime group members
record.detail: State media said 11 people sentenced by a Wenzhou court in Sept 2025, including Ming family criminal group members, were executed after Supreme People's Court approval for homicide, fraud, unlawful detention and casino offences tied to Myanmar scam compounds; 14 Chinese citizens were killed by the group.
record.attribution: Chinese state media via Al Jazeera

record.title: Four Bai family gang leaders executed in Shenzhen
record.detail: Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court executed Bai Yingcang, Yang Liqiang, Hu Xiaojing and Chen Guangyi; boss Bai Suocheng died of illness. The group ran Kokang scam compounds involving over 29 billion yuan and trafficked about 11 t of methamphetamine.
record.attribution: Shenzhen court via Global Times (state media)

record.title: PBOC and seven agencies reaffirm crypto ban, bar offshore yuan stablecoins
record.detail: A joint notice declared virtual-currency business illegal, barred issuing RMB-pegged stablecoins abroad without approval, targeted disguised mining and restricted domestic RWA tokenisation.
record.attribution: People's Bank of China et al. via People's Daily

record.title: MPS: over 1,500 suspects repatriated from Myawaddy KK Park
record.detail: The Ministry of Public Security said 10 China-Myanmar-Thailand repatriation operations returned over 1,500 telecom-fraud suspects from Myawaddy, and more than 630 KK Park buildings were demolished.
record.attribution: Ministry of Public Security via Global Times (state media)

record.title: SPC: 41,000+ returnees from northern Myanmar sentenced
record.detail: The Supreme People's Court said over 41,000 people repatriated from northern Myanmar had been sentenced by end-2025, and 159,000+ telecom/online fraud cases (338,000+ defendants) were concluded nationwide 2021-2025; 16 Ming and Bai gang members were executed.
record.attribution: Supreme People's Court via People's Daily (state media)

record.title: HK Customs finds HK$22m of cocaine hidden in Costa Rican logs
record.detail: Customs found about 30 kg of suspected cocaine, worth about HK$22 million, inside three wood logs shipped from Costa Rica at the Kwai Chung cargo compound on February 10; a controlled delivery led to the arrest of four foreign nationals aged 27-49 in Tsing Yi on February 26.
record.attribution: Per Hong Kong Customs press release

record.title: SPP: 18,376 prosecuted for fake and substandard goods in 2025
record.detail: Ahead of World Consumer Rights Day the SPP said prosecutors approved 5,745 arrests and prosecuted 18,376 people for making or selling counterfeit or substandard goods in 2025, plus 9,595 people in 5,026 food-safety cases and 4,043 in 2,135 drug-safety cases.
record.attribution: Figures per the SPP (government); not independently verified

record.title: Operation Wind Chain: Macau-mainland bust of casino exchange laundering network
record.detail: Macau Judiciary Police said 25 were arrested in Macau and 40 on the mainland over a network that laundered about RMB 45.6m of telecom-fraud proceeds through casino-side currency exchange and USDT; 11 underground banks in Zhuhai were dismantled and HK$5.7m cash seized.
record.agency: Macao Judiciary Police / Ministry of Public Security

record.title: PLA tracks Japanese destroyer Ikazuchi through Taiwan Strait
record.detail: The PLA Eastern Theater Command said naval and air forces tracked JS Ikazuchi throughout its transit; the defence ministry called it a 'deliberate provocation' and lodged a protest with Japan.
record.attribution: PLA Eastern Theater Command via CGTN (state media)

record.title: Explosion at Liuyang fireworks plant kills at least 26
record.detail: An explosion at a fireworks manufacturer in Guandu Town, Liuyang killed at least 26 and injured 61; nearby residents were evacuated because of two black-powder warehouses and police detained the company's person in charge.
record.agency: Changsha municipal government; Ministry of Emergency Management
record.attribution: Casualty figures per Xinhua and CCTV (state media) as reported by AP/NPR; not independently verified

record.title: M5.2 quake in Liuzhou kills 2, collapses 13 buildings
record.detail: A shallow (8 km) M5.2 quake struck Liunan District at 00:21, killing two, hospitalising four and collapsing 13 buildings; more than 7,000 residents were relocated. A Level-IV national emergency response was launched.
record.agency: China Earthquake Networks Center; Ministry of Emergency Management
record.attribution: Figures per CENC and local authorities via Global Times (state media); not independently verified

record.title: Wei family Kokang syndicate goes on trial in Quanzhou
record.detail: Wei Huairen and syndicate members were tried on fraud, murder, extortion and organising illegal border crossings; prosecutors allege victims in China lost over 24 billion yuan and two Chinese citizens were killed.

record.title: Gas blast at Liushenyu coal mine in Shanxi kills 82
record.detail: A gas explosion on the Friday evening shift at the Liushenyu mine in Changzhi (about 247 miners underground) killed 82, a toll revised down from an initial 90, with two missing and more than 120 hospitalised. Officials cited serious violations by the operator and placed those responsible under control; the mine had been flagged as high-gas in 2024.
record.agency: Ministry of Emergency Management; State Council investigation team
record.attribution: Tolls per Xinhua and CCTV (state media) as reported by AP/NPR; state media first reported 90 dead, then revised to 82 (other outlets carried differing figures); not independently verified

record.title: M6.3 quake in Haixi, Qinghai: 1 dead, 8 injured
record.detail: An M6.3 quake at 10 km depth struck Haixi Mongolian and Tibetan Autonomous Prefecture at 17:06; one person died and eight were injured. Thousands were moved to five temporary sites and more than 1,000 rescuers deployed.
record.attribution: Figures per CENC and Xinhua via CGTN (state media); not independently verified. Page dated June 17 gives 'Tuesday', i.e. June 16

record.title: Alleged Jinbei Group figure Liu Ren returned from Cambodia
record.detail: MPS escorted Liu Ren, whom Chinese authorities accuse of a central role in scam and online gambling operations of Chen Zhi's Jinbei Group, from Phnom Penh to China.
record.attribution: Ministry of Public Security claim via Cambodia Investment Review

record.title: HK police arrest 69 for laundering HK$200m of scam proceeds
record.detail: Hong Kong Police, with mainland authorities, arrested 69 people accused of laundering about HK$200 million from cross-border romance-investment scams via mule accounts; over 170 victims.
record.attribution: Hong Kong Police Force via SCMP

record.title: SPP: 1,200+ prosecuted for drug-related money laundering
record.detail: The Supreme People's Procuratorate said over 1,200 people were prosecuted for drug-related money laundering from Jan 2025 to May 2026, including a case laundering 48 million yuan via virtual currency.
record.attribution: Supreme People's Procuratorate via Xinhua (state media)

record.title: MPS: 12,000 drug cases and 10.7 tonnes seized in Jan-May
record.detail: The Ministry of Public Security said police cracked 12,000 drug cases, arrested 18,000 suspects and seized 10.7 tonnes of drugs in the first five months of 2026, and caught 49 overseas drug fugitives.
record.attribution: Figures per MPS via Xinhua (state media); not independently verified

record.title: Shanghai court jails five over 200m-yuan crypto forex scheme
record.detail: Jing'an District court sentenced five people to 2.5-6 years for using cryptocurrency to move over 200 million yuan abroad illegally for clients; SAFE flagged the scheme from unusual transactions.

record.title: NMC warns of record 41-44C heat in northwest China
record.detail: The National Meteorological Center forecast 41-44C in parts of Xinjiang and Inner Mongolia, with Turpan Basin at 46.2C, and 35-41C across Huanghuai and the Yangtze delta, lasting 6-9 days.
record.attribution: National Meteorological Center via China Daily (state media)

record.title: Storms, tornado and dam breach kill 15 in Hubei and Guangxi
record.detail: State media reported at least 15 dead and 9 missing after severe convective storms and tornadoes hit Hubei (Huanggang, Huangshi) and Typhoon Maysak rains flooded Guangxi; a reservoir dam breached and 275 were hurt in Huangzhou district.

record.title: Liulan Reservoir breach in Hengzhou; Guangxi goes to Level I
record.detail: A severe breach at the medium-sized Liulan Reservoir after torrential rain prompted evacuation of residents downstream; Guangxi raised its flood emergency response from Level III to Level I at 11:30.
record.agency: Guangxi flood control authorities; water resources department
record.attribution: Per Xinhua (state media); not independently verified

record.title: China and Japan coast guards face off near Diaoyu/Senkaku
record.detail: China's coast guard said it warned and expelled the Japanese fishing boat Zuihou Maru from 'territorial waters'; Japan said it forced two Chinese ships out after they approached the boat.
record.attribution: China Coast Guard and Japan Coast Guard claims via The Defense Post

record.title: Flood-hit power grid restored in Nanning, Qinzhou, Fangchenggang
record.detail: China Southern Power Grid raised its emergency response to Level II and sent more than 10,000 staff, with crews from Guangdong, to restore lines after heavy rain and flooding in three Guangxi cities; the number of customers cut off was not given.
record.attribution: Per China Southern Power Grid via China News Service (state media); not independently verified

record.title: Fire at Jinjiang shoe factory kills 28
record.detail: Fire broke out on the ground floor of a shoe factory in Jiangtou village around noon with 237 workers inside; 213 were rescued and 28 died (26 found dead, 2 died in hospital). More than 180 firefighters were deployed.
record.attribution: Figures per Chinese state media as reported by Al Jazeera wires; not independently verified

record.title: Typhoon Bavi lands at Yuhuan, Zhejiang after 1.7m evacuated
record.detail: Bavi made landfall late on Jul 11/12 near Yuhuan with sustained winds of about 144 km/h; over 1.7 million were evacuated in Zhejiang and ~34,000 in Shanghai, with flights, ferries and some high-speed rail suspended.
record.attribution: NMC and provincial authorities via AP

record.title: Grid and rail repairs in Zhejiang after Typhoon Bavi
record.detail: After Bavi's landfalls at Yuhuan and Yueqing, state grid crews inspected 266 substations and had restored 80% of the primary grid by 14:00; more than 2,600 rail passengers were stranded at Jiaxing South station.
record.attribution: Per CCTV+ (state media) via Bastille Post; not independently verified

record.title: Red heat-health alerts for Hubei, Chongqing, Inner Mongolia
record.detail: The National Disease Control and Prevention Administration and CMA jointly issued heat health risk alerts, red for Hubei, Chongqing and Inner Mongolia; SW Chongqing forecast above 40C and Wuhan grid hit a record 18.11 GW peak.
record.agency: National Disease Control and Prevention Administration / CMA
record.attribution: NDCPA and CMA via China Daily (state media)

record.title: Landslide buries 10+ buildings in Pengshui, Chongqing
record.detail: About 18,000 cubic m of rock buried more than 10 buildings in Qingyang Village, Taiyuan Town; 8 confirmed dead and 34 missing, 10 rescued, about 1,100 residents evacuated; 30 million yuan allocated for relief.

record.title: CCG says it expelled two Philippine vessels at Scarborough Shoal
record.detail: China Coast Guard spokesman Jiang Lue said two Philippine government vessels ignored warnings and entered 'Chinese jurisdiction' near Huangyan Dao and were driven away, a day after Wang Yi warned Manila at ASEAN talks.
record.attribution: China Coast Guard claim via SCMP

record.title: CCG water cannon used on Philippine fisheries vessel at Scarborough

record.attribution: China Coast Guard claim; video via Reuters

record.title: CCG 'rights-protection patrol' in Diaoyu Islands waters

record.attribution: China Coast Guard statement via China Daily (state media)

record.title: Typhoon Noul lands in Huidong, Guangdong; ~350,000 evacuated
record.detail: Noul, the strongest typhoon to hit China in 2026 so far, made landfall about 03:50 at Pinghai Town, Huidong County; CMA raised emergency response to Level II and 12 cities imposed 'five suspensions'.
record.attribution: CMA and Guangdong emergency management via CGTN (state media)

record.title: About 350 flights cancelled at Hong Kong airport for Typhoon Noul

record.attribution: Figures per Guangdong authorities via Global Times (state media); not independently verified

record.title: China-Australia bust of 90m-cigarette smuggling route via Zhanjiang

record.title: Anti-Scam Centre returns Rp161 billion to victims
record.detail: OJK said the Indonesia Anti-Scam Centre returned Rp161 billion to 1,070 victims; from Nov 22, 2024 to Jan 12, 2026 it logged 432,637 complaints with reported losses of Rp9.1 trillion and blocked Rp436.88 billion.

record.title: Burangrang landslide buries Pasirlangu, 82 missing
record.detail: A rain-triggered landslide and flash flood from Mount Burangrang struck about 30 homes in Pasirlangu village; BNPB initially reported 7 dead and 82 missing.

record.title: BNN busts meth and cannabis networks, 360 kg seized
record.detail: BNN said it dismantled a Golden Triangle-linked meth network in Aceh (160 kg, worth about Rp208 billion) and an Aceh-to-Medan cannabis route (200 kg), arresting suspects in both.

record.title: M6.2 megathrust quake off Pacitan injures 36
record.detail: BMKG recorded a M6.2 quake at 58 km depth off Pacitan at 01:06; local BPBDs reported at least 36 injured and 35 buildings damaged in Pacitan and Bantul.

record.title: Smart Air plane shot at Korowai airstrip, two pilots killed
record.detail: An armed separatist group opened fire on a Smart Air aircraft at Korowai airport, killing both pilots; all 13 passengers were rescued. The Cartenz Peace Task Force blamed two Yahukimo-based KKB battalions.
record.attribution: Cartenz Peace Task Force via Antara

record.title: BBMKG Denpasar warns of extreme weather and high waves in Bali to 17 Feb
record.detail: The Region III meteorology office warned all nine Bali districts of heavy rain, thunderstorms and gusty winds from 11 to 17 February, with 1.25-2.5 m waves in the southern straits and possible floods and landslides.

record.title: Govt speeds return of 4,254 Indonesians from Cambodia
record.detail: Kemlu said 4,254 Indonesians registered with the Phnom Penh embassy from Jan 16 to Feb 15 amid Cambodia's scam crackdown; staged flights ran Feb 16-Mar 4. It said many admitted scam involvement and screening of 3,917 found no trafficking victims.

record.title: Police probe Rp25 trillion laundering tied to illegal gold
record.detail: The National Police, working with PPATK, raided two houses and a jewellery shop in Surabaya and Nganjuk, seizing cash, gold and documents in a probe of about Rp25 trillion allegedly laundered from an illegal West Kalimantan gold mine (2019-2022).

record.title: Bantargebang landfill slide kills 5; Jakarta halts dumping in zone 4A
record.detail: A waste-pile landslide in zone 4A of Jakarta's Bantargebang landfill in Bekasi killed five with four missing; the Environment Minister called it a systemic failure and Governor Pramono Anung halted open dumping in the zone, which receives 7,400-8,000 tonnes a day.

record.title: Health Ministry: 58 measles outbreaks in 14 provinces; health workers told to be vigilant
record.detail: The Health Ministry reported 58 measles outbreaks across 39 districts and cities in 14 provinces by week 11, with about 2,740 early-2026 cases falling sharply; it issued a circular requiring isolation, PPE and 24-hour reporting, and ran outbreak immunisation in 102 districts.

record.title: BPOM approves wider adult use of domestic measles vaccine
record.detail: The food and drug agency approved expanded use of Bio Farma's measles vaccine for at-risk adults such as health workers and travellers from 7 April, citing persistent transmission risk after the year's outbreaks.

record.title: Govt weighs US request for military overflight access
record.detail: Foreign Minister Sugiono said Indonesia is reviewing a US letter of intent seeking overflight access for US military aircraft, weighing sovereignty; Reuters earlier reported the foreign ministry privately warned of security risks.

record.title: 26 foreigners, mostly Filipinos, found in Kuta scam operation
record.detail: Denpasar police raided a Kuta hotel and detained 26 foreigners, mainly Filipinos; the Philippine embassy said its citizens were being held by the syndicate to work as scam operators. Trafficking charges were under consideration.
record.attribution: Police, immigration and Philippine embassy via Antara

record.title: Argo Bromo Anggrek rams stationary KRL at Bekasi Timur; 16 dead
record.detail: The long-distance Argo Bromo Anggrek struck a stopped KRL commuter train at East Bekasi Station on the evening of 27 April, killing 16 and injuring 91; police said the commuter train had been halted by a taxi stalled on a level crossing and are probing human error and signalling faults.

record.title: Jakarta floods hit 115 neighbourhood units
record.detail: Heavy rain overflowed seven rivers including the Ciliwung, Krukut and Pesanggrahan, flooding 115 neighbourhood units (78 in South Jakarta) to depths of 15 cm to 2.4 m, Jakarta BPBD said.

record.title: Densus 88 arrests eight JAD suspects in Central Sulawesi
record.detail: Densus 88 arrested eight suspects linked to IS-affiliated Jamaah Anshoru Daulah, four in Parigi Moutong and four in Poso, alleged to have spread extremist propaganda online, a National Police spokesperson said.

record.title: 210 foreigners detained in Batam fake-trading scam raid
record.detail: Batam immigration and a joint team raided Baloi View apartments, detaining 210 foreigners (125 Vietnamese, 84 Chinese, 1 Myanmar) allegedly running fake stock/forex trading apps targeting victims in Europe and Vietnam; hundreds of devices and 198 passports seized.

record.title: Bareskrim arrests 321 foreigners in online gambling raid
record.detail: Bareskrim said it arrested 321 foreign nationals, mostly Vietnamese (228) and Chinese (57), running an online gambling operation in Jakarta linked to about 75 domains.

record.title: Police report 1,241 counterfeit-money suspects
record.detail: Bareskrim said 252 counterfeit currency cases in 2025-2026 led to 1,241 arrests and seizure of 137,005 fake rupiah and 17,267 fake US dollar notes; it destroyed 466,535 fake notes.

record.title: Firefight in Dekai; TPNPB claims retaliatory killing
record.detail: TPNPB said two of its fighters died in a clash with security forces in Dekai and claimed it shot dead one soldier in retaliation; the soldier's death was not confirmed by Indonesian authorities.
record.attribution: TPNPB claims via Jubi (unconfirmed by TNI/Polri)

record.title: Border task force trains anti-drone surveillance at Entikong
record.detail: The Indonesia-Malaysia Border Security Task Force ran counter-drone drills at Entikong and Temajuk, citing drone risks tied to illegal crossings, smuggling and espionage, its commander said.

record.title: OJK launches National Fraud Portal
record.detail: OJK launched a National Fraud Portal in the Anti-Scam Centre; it reported 14,232 complaints Jan-Apr 29, 2026 (11,753 on illegal online loans) and 951 illegal lending entities shut by the PASTI task force.

record.title: Pig-butchering ring busted in Sukoharjo, 39 suspects
record.detail: Central Java police named 39 suspects, including 11 from Nepal and Myanmar, in a romance-crypto fraud ring that allegedly took about Rp41.1 billion from 133 mostly US victims between Jul 2025 and May 2026.

record.title: Two gold refiner directors detained in illegal-gold laundering case
record.detail: Bareskrim detained a former and the current director of a gold company on suspicion of processing and selling gold from illegal mines and money laundering, adding to three suspects from a Nganjuk gold business; PPATK is tracing assets.

record.title: US pilot killed as mission aircraft shot at in Yahukimo
record.detail: Gunmen fired on an Associated Mission Aviation (AMA) aircraft flying Wamena to Balinggama, killing its American pilot. The Cartenz task force attributed the attack to a newly emerged 'Bakusip' faction.
record.attribution: Cartenz Peace Task Force via Antara

record.title: Repatriation requests from Cambodia hit 11,986 in H1
record.detail: Kemlu's citizen-protection director said 11,986 Indonesians requested repatriation from Cambodia in Jan-Jun 2026, more than double the 5,088 in all of 2025, as Cambodia raided scam compounds.

record.title: Rolling blackouts hit Java-Bali grid; government orders PLN fixes
record.detail: Rolling blackouts in mid-2026 hit millions on the Java-Bali grid, including South Tangerang and Depok; PLN blamed a shortage of suitable-grade coal. On 3 July the government ordered PLN to secure fuel supply and speed generator maintenance. Asia Times reported emergency coal shipments later ended the rolling cuts.
record.agency: PLN / Energy and Mineral Resources Ministry
record.attribution: Asia Times; government order per ANTARA (en.antaranews.com/news/421431)

record.title: OJK: 557,000 suspected scam accounts blocked
record.detail: OJK said the Anti-Scam Centre had blocked over 557,000 suspected accounts from 608,000+ scam reports as of June 2026, freezing Rp674 billion and returning about Rp200 billion.
record.attribution: OJK figures via Fintech News Indonesia

record.title: BMKG: Cyclone Bavi brings strong winds and 4 m waves to eastern Indonesia
record.detail: BMKG said Tropical Cyclone Bavi, north of Papua and moving west, threatened strong winds in North Sulawesi, North Maluku, Southwest Papua and West Papua, with waves of 2.5-4.0 m north of Maluku and West Papua.
record.place: Waters north of Papua and Maluku

record.title: TNI AU and RMAF fly joint border air patrol
record.detail: Two Indonesian F-16s and two Malaysian F/A-18s flew the Malindo coordinated patrol along the shared maritime border, the TNI AU spokesperson said.

record.title: 32,500 gambling-linked bank accounts closed
record.detail: Komdigi said 3.7 million gambling sites/content were blocked and 38,000 suspected gambling-linked accounts referred, of which 32,500 were closed (Oct 20, 2024-Jul 12, 2026); PPATK data put 2025 online-gambling transactions at Rp286.84 trillion.

record.title: BNN: 1,259 drug arrests in 2026 across 34 provinces
record.detail: BNN head Suyudi Ario Seto said 2026 operations produced 1,259 arrests, 126.3 kg of meth, a 3.37 t cannabis interception in Gresik and a mephedrone lab bust in Bali; the agency cited 12.3 t seized over 21 months.

record.title: M7.7 quake off Flores kills at least 47
record.detail: A magnitude 7.7 quake at 10 km depth struck about 68 km NNW of Ende, killing at least 47, destroying 157 houses and damaging about 200; a tsunami warning was issued then lifted and about 2,000 villagers in Nagekeo evacuated.

record.title: 2.6 t liquid meth seized from Tanzanian-flagged ship
record.detail: BNN, Customs and Riau Islands police intercepted the MV Ocean Porter in Riau waters with 2.6 tons of liquid methamphetamine, arresting 10 Myanmar crew; officials said the cargo was tied to trafficking from Sarawak.

record.title: Navy says 514 t of illegal minerals seized in 2026
record.detail: The Fleet Command said it seized 514.1 tons of illegally mined minerals (tin sand, coal) worth Rp10.25 trillion so far in 2026, incl. 75.7 t of tin sand off Bangka Belitung on Aug 2-13, and 1.3 t of drugs.

record.title: Govt marks fourth year without terror attack
record.detail: Deputy Coordinating Minister Lodewijk F. Paulus said Indonesia had entered a fourth year with zero terrorist attacks; BNPT head Eddy Hartono said 28 planned attacks were thwarted over four years.

record.title: About 475 Indonesians held in Phnom Penh after scam crackdown
record.detail: At least 475 Indonesians who had worked in Cambodian scam operations were held at a facility near Pochentong airport awaiting repatriation; detainees said embassy support ended Aug 30 for lack of funds.

record.title: BNPB: 1,730 disasters Jan 1-Sep 7
record.detail: BNPB reported 1,730 disasters from Jan 1 to Sep 7, 2026, led by wildfires (627), floods (543), extreme weather (324), landslides (105) and droughts (101), plus 13 major earthquakes and 3 volcanic eruptions; 111,533 homes damaged.

record.detail: The Surabaya-Banjarmasin ferry Virgo Transport 8, carrying 243 people, capsized in 3-metre waves near the Masalembo islands; by 25 September BASARNAS divers had recovered 52 bodies, 108 were rescued and 83 remained missing.

record.detail: The Geological Agency lowered Anak Krakatau from Level III to Level II from Sep 21 after the Sep 4-6 eruptions, which it said formed two new islets and expanded the edifice by 32.8 ha; 2 km crater and 1 km islet exclusion zones apply.

record.detail: A bus carrying 66 passengers from Solan skidded off a mountain road into a deep gorge near Haripurdhar; state minister Jagat Singh Negi put the toll at 14 with about 40 injured. Xinhua reported the crash on Friday (9 January); its article is dated 10 January.

record.detail: Troops fired at drone-like objects that crossed the LoC near Dunga Gala (Chingus) and Dheri Dhara in Rajouri; they returned to PoK and searches for airdrops followed. Similar activity was reported days earlier in Rajouri, Poonch and Samba.

record.title: Two Nipah cases confirmed among health workers in Barasat, West Bengal
record.detail: WHO reported two laboratory-confirmed Nipah virus cases, both healthcare workers, confirmed 13 January in Barasat; over 190 contacts tested negative. WHO rated risk moderate sub-nationally and low nationally and globally.

record.title: Shah reviews LWE in Raipur, reiterates March 31 deadline
record.detail: At a Raipur review, Home Minister Amit Shah said Naxalism would be eradicated before 31 March 2026 and cited 500+ Naxalites killed, about 1,900 arrested and 2,500+ surrendered since January 2024.

record.detail: After US and Israeli strikes on Iran, Air India and IndiGo suspended all Middle East flights and Air India Express its Gulf flights until 1 March, offering refunds and free rebooking.

record.title: Infiltration bid foiled at Bhimber Gali on LoC
record.detail: The Army said terrorist movement was detected in the Bhimber Gali area in early morning and troops prevented a breach; alert heightened along the LoC and IB.

record.title: ED has 257 cyber-crime PMLA cases, Rs 35,925 crore proceeds
record.detail: The government told Parliament that as of 28 Feb 2026 ED had 257 cybercrime-linked PMLA cases with Rs 35,925.58 crore identified proceeds; the suspect registry had blocked Rs 9,518.91 crore and the I4C fraud reporting system recovered over Rs 8,690 crore. Source gives only "March 2026"; the day is a placeholder.

record.title: Rs 23.72 crore meth found in truck near Myanmar border
record.detail: Assam Rifles and Mizoram Police found 7.907 kg of methamphetamine tablets worth Rs 23.72 crore in an abandoned truck on Hmunhmeltha Road; officials suspect origin in Myanmar's Chin State.

record.title: RBI expands MuleHunter.AI, revises e-banking fraud rules
record.detail: RBI said it revised its 2017 rules on unauthorised electronic transactions (draft issued 6 Mar 2026) and that its MuleHunter.AI tool to detect mule accounts is live in 26 banks and expanding.

record.title: ED attaches Rs 1,700 crore Dubai, Delhi assets in Mahadev case
record.detail: ED attached 18 Dubai and 2 Delhi properties worth Rs 1,700 crore linked to Mahadev betting app promoter Sourabh Chandrakar; it cites 175+ searches and 13 arrests so far.

record.title: Government declares India free of Maoist insurgency
record.detail: Home Minister Amit Shah told Parliament India was free of Naxalites, while saying all but two Maoist commanders had been killed or surrendered; he cited 364 insurgents killed, 1,022 arrested and 2,337 surrendered in 2025.
record.attribution: Government claim by Amit Shah via AFP

record.title: Police raid 'mini Jamtara' cyber-fraud village near Kanpur
record.detail: Police using drone surveillance raided Reuna village, Ghatampur, arresting 20 (15 escaped); callers allegedly posed as officials offering loans or housing schemes, and SIM cards, laptops and evidence of 20-50 mule accounts were seized.

record.title: CBI arrests bank official, two others in Rs 1.6 crore digital-arrest case
record.detail: CBI searched five locations in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh and arrested three people including a bank official over a Rs 1.6 crore digital-arrest fraud on a senior citizen; mule accounts and layered transactions were found.

record.title: Mini-bus of Kerala tourists falls into gorge in Tamil Nadu; 10 dead
record.detail: A mini-bus carrying 16 people from Kerala on a leisure trip fell into a deep gorge in Tamil Nadu, killing at least 10, per Xinhua citing All India Radio; police opened a case.
record.place: Tamil Nadu hills (exact site not given)

record.title: Firecracker factory blast kills 21 in Virudhunagar
record.detail: An explosion while workers moved flammable chemicals destroyed a fireworks factory at V. Muthulingapuram, killing 21 and injuring 6, per Xinhua citing All India Radio; about 50 labourers were inside.

record.title: Delhi hottest day of year at 42.8C; heatwave alerts across north and east
record.detail: Safdarjung hit 42.8C, 5.1C above normal; IMD issued orange alert for Delhi and heatwave warnings for J&K, HP, Punjab, Haryana, UP, MP, Vidarbha, Chhattisgarh, Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha.

record.title: Two Bangladeshis killed in BSF firing in Sepahijala
record.detail: BSF said a group challenged at the zero line in Sepahijala district pelted troops with stones and that personnel fired pump-action guns in self-defence; two men died in hospital.

record.title: Army kills intruder in Krishna Ghati sector, Poonch
record.detail: The Army's White Knight Corps said one intruder was neutralised after being detected about 300 m inside Indian territory near Mankote; sources linked him to Lashkar-e-Taiba.

record.title: Bangladeshi cattle-lifting suspect killed in Cooch Behar
record.detail: BSF said troops fired after repeated warnings at 10-12 intruders crossing near border pillar 905 in Cooch Behar district to lift cattle; one was killed.

record.title: Heatwave kills over 100 in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
record.detail: Khaleej Times reported over 100 heat deaths across the two states, including 23 in Warangal in one day, with highs of 48.3C at Chityala; Telangana's revenue minister ordered early warnings and cold-water points, and IMD warned heat would continue in the north.

record.title: India-China WMCC talks in Beijing on LAC
record.detail: The Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination met in Beijing; MEA called talks constructive and said both sides would prepare for the next Special Representatives meeting and hold expert talks on trans-border rivers.

record.title: Under-construction Betwa River bridge collapses in storm; 6 workers dead
record.detail: Police and officials said an under-construction bridge over the Betwa linking Morakandar and Kandaur villages collapsed during a late-night storm on Thursday 28 May, killing six labourers and injuring three.

record.title: MEA: 2,400+ Indians repatriated from Myanmar scam compounds
record.detail: The MEA said more than 2,400 Indians had been repatriated from cyber scam compounds in Myanmar while about 150 remained trapped.

record.title: BSF recovers 18 kg drone-dropped heroin in Amritsar
record.detail: BSF detected drone activity and recovered about 18 kg of heroin near BOPs Ramkot and Kakkar in the Lopoke sector; no arrests at time of reporting.

record.title: Monsoon reaches Kerala late; IMD forecasts 90% of LPA
record.detail: The southwest monsoon reached Kerala on 4 June, three days after normal and nine days after IMD's forecast of 26 May; IMD forecast below-normal rain at 90% of LPA amid developing El Nino.
record.attribution: IMD forecast via Down To Earth

record.title: ICU fire at private hospital in Muzaffarpur kills 5
record.detail: A pre-dawn fire in the ICU of a private hospital in Muzaffarpur killed five and burned 20; local media blamed a short circuit, per Xinhua.

record.title: ED searches over 36,000 Indian SIMs active in Cambodia
record.detail: ED searched seven sites in Kishangarh, Jodhpur, Nagpur and Ludhiana under PMLA over misuse of SIM cards by point-of-sale vendors; it said 36,000 Indian SIMs were active in Cambodia, 5,300 linked to fraud cases, and 30 bank accounts were identified.

record.title: CBI arrests two over trafficking youth to Myanmar/Cambodia scam compounds
record.detail: CBI arrested two alleged key traffickers in Delhi; one allegedly arranged transit to Myanmar via Thailand and the other ran an office inside a scam compound near the Thai-Myanmar border, managing sub-agents and taking crypto payments.

record.title: Pune moves to alternate-day water supply as delayed monsoon drains dams
record.detail: Pune Municipal Corporation cut supply from 1,600 to 1,100 million litres a day with alternate-day service, and Pimpri-Chinchwad also imposed cuts, as the monsoon stalled about 200 km from the city.

record.title: ED attaches Rs 940.77 crore more in Mahadev betting probe
record.detail: ED provisionally attached property, land and securities worth Rs 940.77 crore of a businessman and associated entities in the Mahadev Online Book/Skyexchange case, taking the total attached, seized or frozen to about Rs 3,800 crore.

record.title: Flash flood in Rajouri; 15 rain deaths in Jammu region
record.detail: A flash flood in Rajouri caused extensive damage; a senior police official said 15 people died in rain-related incidents in Poonch, Rajouri and Doda, with several missing and 11 rescued by Army and state responders.
record.attribution: Senior police official via Al Jazeera

record.title: Landslides kill 9 in Nagaland's Mon district
record.detail: The Mon district magistrate said 9 people were killed and at least 15 injured in landslides; 4 of 8 bodies had been recovered as rescue continued.
record.attribution: Mon district magistrate via Al Jazeera

record.title: Deep depression floods north Odisha; 1 lakh+ affected
record.detail: Over 1 lakh people were affected in Balasore, Jajpur, Bhadrak and Mayurbhanj, with 23,650+ relocated and about 300 houses damaged; Balasore logged 246 mm in 24 h. Lightning killed 3 in Chhattisgarh's MCB district.
record.attribution: State officials and IMD via ETV Bharat

record.title: Residential building collapse in Bhiwandi kills at least 9
record.detail: Local officials said a multi-storey residential building collapsed in Bhiwandi near Mumbai, killing at least nine with others trapped as rescue continued overnight.

record.title: Monsoon floods and landslides kill 100+ since July
record.detail: Official data cited by Al Jazeera put Assam deaths at 87 (47 in Sivasagar district), Kerala at 15 with 7 missing and 10,000+ in 300+ relief camps, and J&K at 31 from intense rain bursts.
record.attribution: State officials and broadcaster figures via Al Jazeera

record.title: Lightning kills 14 farm workers in Jharkhand
record.detail: IMD-cited figures reported by Al Jazeera said 14 people, mainly farm workers in open fields, were killed by lightning in Jharkhand during the monsoon.

record.title: ~500 Rajasthan youths went to SE Asian scam centres: police
record.detail: A Rajasthan State Cyber Police officer, citing I4C inputs, said about 500 youths from the state had travelled to scam centres in Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam; about eight repeat travellers have been arrested and Beawar, Shekhawati and Udaipur are being monitored.

record.title: Firecracker unit blast in Kaushambi kills 11, including 8 children
record.detail: Police said an explosion at a firecracker factory in Kaushambi district collapsed nearby houses, killing at least 11 people including eight children; the cause was unclear.

record.title: Pastor shot, homes burned in Kangpokpi village
record.detail: Human Rights Watch reported that a pastor was shot and homes were burned in Old Tapon village, Kangpokpi district, amid Naga-Kuki clashes.

record.title: HRW: 34 dead in Manipur Naga-Kuki violence since February
record.detail: Human Rights Watch said renewed Naga vs Kuki-Zo violence killed 34 people since February 2026, including at least 7 in late August; 48 people were reportedly abducted in May after three Kuki church leaders were killed.

record.title: CBI Operation Chakra-VI hits 89 digital-arrest sites in 20 states
record.detail: CBI searched 89 locations across 20 states against digital-arrest syndicates and arrested three people accused of receiving and moving fraud proceeds through purpose-opened bank accounts; linked cases total about Rs 42.36 crore (Gujarat Rs 19.24 cr, Karnataka Rs 15.45 cr, Rajasthan Rs 7.67 cr).

record.title: Meth tablets worth Rs 5.59 crore seized at Seling
record.detail: Assam Rifles and NCB Aizawl intercepted two vehicles and seized 6.991 kg of methamphetamine tablets valued at about Rs 5.59 crore; two arrested.

record.title: Deep depression crosses coast near Kalingapatnam
record.detail: A Bay of Bengal deep depression crossed near Kalingapatnam overnight 23-24 Sept; over 8,000 were evacuated (about 5,000 to 264 shelters in Gajapati), one died in a house collapse in Balasore, and IMD kept red warnings for Koraput, Malkangiri, Kalahandi and Nabarangpur to 25 Sept.
record.attribution: IMD and state officials via ETV Bharat
